title: Read or match the solution on a graph
subtitle: Systems of two linear equations in two variables · 13 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **13 of the official questions in Systems of two linear equations in two variables are this one** — 7 Easy, 4 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You are shown a graph of two lines, or of two functions modelling a situation.
- The question asks for the solution to the system, or asks which pair of equations or functions the graphed lines could be.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) For 'what is the solution', find the single point where the lines cross and read its (x, y) from the gridlines.
- 2) For 'which equations could these be', read the y-intercept and slope of each line from two clear lattice points.
- Keep only the choice whose slopes and intercepts match both lines, including the sign of each slope.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: For matching questions, graph each answer choice and compare it with the picture.
Or type in points read off the graph and fit a line through them.
For reading an intersection, you don't need Desmos: just read the graph.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a point that lies on only one of the lines, such as its intercept, instead of the crossing point.
When matching, you pair the right slope with the wrong intercept, or mix up which line is increasing.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
